paper: Dong et al., How to Continually Adapt Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Flexible Customization?, arXiv:2410.17594, NeurIPS 2024
box_convention: (x0, y0, x1, y1) normalised to the figure panel frame, origin TOP-LEFT -- the same convention as src.regional._region_vec

provenance.itp_rtp: transcribed verbatim from the text layer of the arXiv e-print figure PDFs; the spacing quirks and the missing full stop in 12.5 are the authors'
provenance.boxes: measured from the vector rectangles of the Region Boxes panel, rounded to 3 dp
provenance.pairing: concept-to-box by rectangle colour and label position, NOT by the order of the RTP string -- the two differ in 3.2, 3.4, 3.5 and 12.1
provenance.region_order: regions are listed left to right by box x0, i.e. reading order in the figure

our_side.region_prompt: the RTP segment with the V<k> label removed and an article prepended, trailing full stop dropped. Nothing else is added -- the scene context some segments carry (walking on the street) is the authors', and segments that carry none stay bare.
our_side.class_word: token span used for the LoRA token mask inside region_prompt

scenes.conflict: RESOLVED 2026-09-14 BY THE FIGURE ITSELF, not by inference. Both the RTP and the box label read V9 dog while the dataset defines V9 as a cat. CIDM's own Ours panel for this row renders a DOG in the right-hand box -- a small smooth-coated corgi in a spacesuit, matching the Task 7 (V7) thumbnail, and visually distinct from the large fluffy V1 corgi in the middle box. The grey Russian Blue of the Task 9 (V9) thumbnail appears nowhere in the panel. So V9 is a labelling error for V7 in both the RTP and the box label. The 'v9' and 'literal' readings stay in alternatives and are reachable with --scene35, for reproducing the figure as printed.
